grounding-01.headline: Ground facts and memory in time, meaning, access and source health
grounding-01.lead: Financial context is a changing information set, not a bag of relevant passages. A request needs an entity, decision, period and cutoff; persistent knowledge additionally needs evidence age, contradictions and a way to accept corrections.

insights.title: Set the evidence boundary
insights.text: Bridgewater’s Vault organizes research by source, market, country, concept and discussed period. Apply entitlements and time constraints before synthesis. A correct answer to a neighboring period, entity or definition is still a failure of the requested task.

insights.title: Preserve changing beliefs
insights.text: Citadel Securities separates reported project status from evidence-based status, keeps historical records, ages claims and compares earlier predictions with later outcomes. Models propose updates; code and people decide what enters the record. This is richer than retrieving the latest matching sentence.

insights.title: Treat missing signals honestly
insights.text: A quiet source can mean a collection problem rather than inactivity. Preserve last observed time, source health and correction history; unknown is not zero. Our combined evidence contract adds versioned definitions and as-of snapshots, without claiming a single firm implemented every field.

grounding-02.headline: Evaluate eligible evidence coverage separately from human-facing relevance
grounding-02.lead: Bridgewater supplies a concrete retrieval-learning loop: label relevant and plausible irrelevant evidence, reproduce complaints, and test filtering under the constraints found in real use. Larger context alone is not the objective.

insights.title: Make relevance observable
insights.text: The speakers describe roughly 200 manually labeled questions and a reported precision@10 rise from about 60% to 90–95%. The speaker corrects an initial “recall” reference to precision. This is an internal retrieval comparison, not measured final-answer quality or investment performance.

insights.title: Test restrictive filters
insights.text: Post-filtering can discard eligible candidates after vector search; exhaustive pre-filtered scoring can be slow. Evaluate combinations of time, source and asset constraints, including sparse matches and no evidence. Measure coverage and latency rather than choosing an index from a generic benchmark.

insights.title: Design for the consumer
insights.text: An agent may collect broad evidence while a human needs a small reviewable brief. Assess both stages: required-source coverage before compression, then retained meaning and review effort. Saved searches, collections and familiar-channel migration are part of adoption, not merely interface decoration.

grounding-03.headline: Resolve numbers through facts and code, then verify the final claim
grounding-03.lead: Kepler distinguishes a wrong source, a wrong fact inside the right source and a wrong calculation. Its released accounts add a constrained number path; final generation still needs checks after retrieval and arithmetic.

insights.title: Use a structured fact
insights.text: The standalone breakout description names value, unit, scale and period. The next-day transcript describes fact identifiers resolved by software while a model plans. Preserve the source anchor and calculation inputs; a valid identifier still needs the correct entity, definition and version.

insights.title: Keep access on every path
insights.text: Exact lookup does not bypass authorization. Search, direct reads, calculation inputs and output references must remain within the user and tenant scope. Test revoked access and empty evidence as well as the successful path; a citation chip does not enforce permission.

insights.title: Verify what the user receives
insights.text: The main-stage transcript explicitly retains post-processing because generation can invent numbers afterward. The breakout description says unverifiable figures are stripped. Our requirement is stronger: correct, remove or escalate the unsupported material claim, rather than leave persuasive prose with broken support.

grounding-04.headline: Correct arithmetic can produce the wrong answer when the source is stale
grounding-04.lead: This synthetic AsterCo example separates calculation correctness from source validity: preliminary revenue produces 18% growth, while the final source available at the requested cutoff produces 20%.

insights.title: Apply the information cutoff
insights.text: All company data and documents here are invented. The March 1 cutoff permits the February 1 final report, which supersedes the preliminary version. Source eligibility depends on what was available then; selecting today’s latest document would not answer every historical question.

insights.title: Recompute the dependent claim
insights.text: Using preliminary revenue of 118 against prior-year revenue of 100 gives 18%; using final revenue of 120 gives 20%. Both calculations are arithmetically valid. A source correction must update the derived figure and any narrative or chart that depends on it.

insights.title: Preserve the rejected version
insights.text: Retain the chosen inputs, publication dates, calculation, and reason the preliminary source was superseded. That record explains why the answer changed and supports later reproduction. Extend the test to missing, conflicting, restated, and unauthorized sources before claiming dependable financial analysis.

grounding-05.headline: Evidence and corrections must survive into the document people actually use
grounding-05.lead: Financial work often ends in a workbook, report or presentation. Inspectable chat output is insufficient if an export loses provenance, carries an old calculation or hides a contradictory period in a polished chart.

insights.title: Preserve the claim chain
insights.text: OpenAI’s finance presentation connects source passages and tables to charts and reusable artifacts. Carry the material value, period, unit and source into the deliverable. Reconcile the document with the current evidence after a correction rather than treating export as a cosmetic step.

insights.title: Check collaborative scope
insights.text: Compound AI describes shared deal threads, an agent inbox and longer artifact work. Permissions must follow participants and source material, not only the connector. Inspect workbook depth, file coverage and final fidelity separately; vendor architecture is not independently verified Office parity.

insights.title: Review the current saved artifact
insights.text: Use a write–render–check–fix loop and inspect again after the final edit. Our acceptance contract checks the actual report the team will share, including stale sources, truncated tables and missing caveats. Passing code or an older preview cannot establish that the current artifact is usable.

workflows-01.headline: Expert skills need reasons, stopping conditions, ownership and independent review
workflows-01.lead: Range’s released account turns the five-step process into a maintained operating practice. The skill expresses professional judgment in a form agents can reuse; people remain responsible for its validity and for client-facing recommendations.

insights.title: Pick and teach a whole task
insights.text: Choose repeated work whose success a professional can recognize. Use prior cases to explain what information matters, how the firm reasons and why a branch exists. A recording of clicks without the reason cannot reliably guide a new or incomplete situation.

insights.title: Pack the boundaries
insights.text: Include required inputs, clarification questions, exceptions, stopping conditions and the handoff. Test missing facts and conflicting instructions as well as ordinary completion. The speaker’s five-to-ten-case routine starts iteration; it does not demonstrate statistical reliability or replace broader assessment.

insights.title: Ship with maintenance
insights.text: Assign an owner and a separate reviewer, keep the method current and retest changes. Range’s agent sends nothing and every recommendation is reviewed by a planner. Measure corrected, accepted work before claiming capacity gains; the transcript provides a method rather than a controlled outcome study.

workflows-02.headline: Let agents iterate inside a stage; require explicit evidence to advance
workflows-02.lead: Coinbase’s framework places bounded draft/check/refine loops inside a forward-moving policy workflow. Drafting, professional judgment and execution authority remain different decisions, even when one interface makes the work feel continuous.

insights.title: Define the stage contract
insights.text: Specify the allowed inputs, checkable output, iteration budget and human takeover condition. The loop can improve a draft while the outer workflow waits for the required acceptance or approval. Faster generation can shift the bottleneck to review rather than remove it.

insights.title: Keep professional judgment visible
insights.text: The invented annual packet below subtracts $84k recorded expenses from $120k income: $36k is only an arithmetic difference. It establishes neither disposable capacity nor suitability. Review the facts, gaps, assumptions and conclusions before the work can be considered accepted.

insights.title: Separate review from permission
insights.text: Range preserves planner review; Perpetual binds approval to an exact payload. Accepting a draft is not permission to send or transact. A separate enforcing boundary checks user, case, resource and action, and retains the approval and outcome evidence.

workflows-03.headline: Enforce identity, scope and stopping conditions outside the agent
workflows-03.lead: Two Sigma’s ownership/access framing and Bloomberg’s execution defenses meet at one point: the model can propose an action, but an enforcing service must decide whether it can happen.

insights.title: Make the agent accountable
insights.text: Register an owner, purpose, tools and accessible resources. Use short-lived scoped identity and carry the user’s authority through the tool path. A valid credential or schema does not establish that a business action is appropriate for this case.

insights.title: Test the actual boundary
insights.text: Challenge cross-tenant queries, revoked access, agent-to-agent privilege escalation, retries and budget exhaustion. Bloomberg recommends deterministic invocation checks and egress limits including DNS. Verify that a denied action is blocked and a halt condition stops execution, rather than merely producing an alert.

insights.title: Treat memory as an input surface
insights.text: A hostile document can try to persist an instruction for a future run. Separate source content from trusted procedure, control memory writes and preserve provenance. Independent approval triage can reduce attention demands only if its errors and enforcement role are understood; it cannot silently waive required approval.

workflows-04.headline: Make verification cheap at creation and independent at release and operation
workflows-04.lead: Sonar’s three-loop framing becomes useful when each loop has a distinct job. Capital One adds a complementary lesson: standard infrastructure can reduce the cost of engineering rigor instead of leaving verification to a late manual cleanup.

insights.title: Creation: prevent and inspect
insights.text: Supply intent, constraints, shared test fixtures and fast low-noise checks while work is generated. Keep deterministic checks for properties that can be asserted exactly. Another model’s agreement or a quick approval does not replace independent evidence of correctness.

insights.title: Release: verify the complete change
insights.text: Test interfaces, permissions, financial invariants and representative regressions. Inspect the current saved artifact after the last edit. Keep the evidence and the decision owner together; a check that can be bypassed or does not halt the relevant action is an incomplete gate.

insights.title: Operation: reproduce and repair
insights.text: Capture escaped failures, reconstruct their context and verify the repair against other work. The confidence product in Sonar’s talk is conceptual, and its code-size illustration is workload-specific. Neither supplies a calibrated assurance formula or a universal limit on agent-generated software.

workflows-05.headline: Long-running financial work needs durable state and deliberate recovery
workflows-05.lead: Arca and Perpetual supply complementary mechanisms: persist the shared plan across real-world waits, then constrain the execution transitions and side effects. Long horizon is a workflow property, not simply a larger context window.

insights.title: Persist the handoff
insights.text: Keep the goal, approved plan, completed work, evidence and next responsible party outside a disposable run. Wake on a client reply, approval, settlement event or deadline. A new invocation should know what happened and what remains, without assuming every prior action failed.

insights.title: Freeze the approved action
insights.text: Perpetual separates provisional interpretation from a compiled plan and binds approval to the exact outgoing payload. Clarification or refusal can be correct outcomes. Changes to a client reply must not silently rewrite the approved parent plan or inherit permission for a different action.

insights.title: Distinguish unknown from failed
insights.text: A timeout after an external write can leave the outcome unknown. Blind retries can duplicate an action. Route uncertainty to reconciliation or manual review; test interruptions around the side-effect boundary. Vanguard’s separate modernization story reinforces invariants and observability, not unconstrained autonomy.
